text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT 2067001234  LATENCY SPIKE (p95/p99) on /v1/streaming/generate  paging oncall
sara: paging oncall  customers in EU/US seeing 100-500ms extra per-token; p99 up to 3.2s for streaming tail, p95 ~800ms. Getting several support tickets about partial streams + client reconnects. :rotating_light:
alex: seeing a big uptick in control-plane errors in the tail path when we hit config fetch for per-org flags. Logs show timeouts to ff-service and auth-service around the same time.
priya: confirmed  dashboard: 30% increase in calls to /config/fetch and 12% 5xx from ff-service. DB connections at 95% for configstore replicas.
ops_lead: priority: P1 until we confirm customer impact. Sara, you\u2019re oncall right now; lead the handoff. Alex, can you attach quick evidence (queries, stacktraces)?
sara: I'm on it. noting initial mitigation: rolled forward a short-lived retry backoff on streaming proxy to reduce retry storms. Notified Support to pause wide-scale restarts from customers.
alex: past 5m snippet: ```
[2026-02-10T14:03:22Z] stream_req id=abc123 stage=config-fetch dur=1200ms err=timeout
[2026-02-10T14:03:22Z] auth token refresh id=auth-req-9 dur=850ms rate_limit=true
[2026-02-10T14:03:23Z] ff-service GET /org/987654 config-miss cache=false dur=1600ms
``` 
alex: stacktrace points to connection queue waits in configstore client, waiting on DB pool.
priya: hypothesize: recent rollout of per-tenant feature flags causes N+1 config fetches per streaming start, causing DB hot connections and cascading auth token refreshes (since some calls require validating tokens for config visibility).
jordan: any recent deploys? I see a canary of 'ff-multi-tenant' merged 40m ago to prod.
sara: rollback request sent for ff-multi-tenant canary  awaiting approval. Meanwhile need traffic-level mitigations.
ops_lead: mitigation plan (short list): 1) add proxy-level config cache (30s TTL) 2) throttle per-org config fetch to 5r/s 3) fallback streaming path that skips config fetch (graceful degrade) 4) increase configstore DB pool by 20% on replicas 5) engage DB oncall if connection saturation persists
alex: implementing proxy cache now  pushing patch to streaming-proxy conf to cache per-org config for 60s and enable stale-while-revalidate. Will push in 2m.
priya: I'll open a SQL connection scaling ticket and run `SHOW PROCESSLIST` on replica-1 to find long-running queries.
priya: quick telemetry: auth-service returning 429 for token refreshes for some clients  looks like per-second burst limiter is tripping because config fetches increment auth usage.
sara: Support update: flagged top 5 paying customers affected (customer_A, customer_B)  offering incident notification. We need to estimate duration and customer impact class.
ops_lead: set Severity: S2 for now but move to S1 if errors persist or if >10% of traffic degraded. Log on incident channel and update status page draft.
jordan: pushed the proxy cache config, verifying: ```curl -X POST http://stream-proxy/config/reload -d '{"file": "/etc/stream-proxy/cache.toml"}'```

jordan: reload returned 200, cache enabled. Observability: config fetch calls reduced by ~40% across streaming path within 30s.
priya: DB processlist shows several `SELECT * FROM configs WHERE org_id = ?` queries stuck in 'Sending data' time > 10s; some prepared statements not using index.

alex: quick short-term ops: increasing DB replica pool by 25% helped connection queue fall to 40% utilization. Still seeing auth 429s occasionally.

sara: rolling out fallback streaming path (skip-config) to 5% of traffic now. This returns best-effort default flags to keep streams flowing. Starting canary.

incident-bot: ONCALL HANDOFF: sara -> jordan in 30m per rotation schedule. Please confirm.

jordan: confirmed. I'll take primary after 30m. Also enabling temporary global rate-limiter for config fetches at edge to 100r/s to stop bursts.

ops_lead: decision log: 1) approved rollback if canary rollback completes and proves less error-prone. 2) enable cache permanently for streaming-proxy if no regressions. 3) DB index ticket created for configs.org_id composite index. 4) post-incident action: audit feature-flag rollout process to prevent N+1.

priya: SQL ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/DB-9987 created; assigned to db-team.

sara: customer comms draft: "We saw temporary streaming tail latency increases affecting partial streams for a subset of customers. Root cause: increased control-plane load (config fetch / feature flags) leading to configstore DB saturation and cascading auth rate-limits. Mitigations: proxy cache, request throttling, DB pool scaling, fallback path. We expect full recovery in 1-2 hours. Apologies for the disruption."

ops_lead: timeline note: incident opened 2026-02-10T14:03Z; mitigation steps active by 14:12Z; canary traffic reroute and DB scaling at 14:15Z; observed p95 back to baseline by 14:25Z; p99 improving but still slightly elevated at 14:30Z.

alex: monitoring: p95 now ~220ms, p99 ~650ms (down from 800ms/3.2s) after mitigations.

jordan: I'll keep an eye during handoff window and escalate to DB oncall if connection queue > 60% again.

sara: switching to postmortem mode after handoff. Thanks team. :heart:
